content.comment_body: Hello, I'm transitioning from a competitor's product to [product_name], and it's going well so far. Is it possible to have two [product_name] units (version [version_no]) located on separate LANs in different locations communicate over the internet? From what I've gathered in various [document], this seems feasible, but I haven't found clear instructions or managed to make it work yet. Any assistance is appreciated.

If the [product_name] units are not within the same subnet, you'll need to use a gateway. There are multiple options for setting up networks with [product_name] units: 1. Create a network project using Drag&Drop. 2. Set up the network project by manually configuring the connection. 3. Use individual LSC files and configure the connection manually. Please provide further details such as IP addresses, subnet masks, etc. for more specific help.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is moving from a competing product to [product_name] (version [version_no]) and wants these devices to communicate over the internet between separate LANs. The main challenge is insufficient or unclear documentation for this network setup, making users unsure about both the capabilities and configuration process for the product.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks clear, step-by-step instructions and documentation to facilitate internet-based communication between [product_name] units (version [version_no]) on different LANs. The user expects comprehensive support for typical networking configurations.
